extracted.intended_audience: consumers, businesses that market AI products or services, journalists, and regulated entities subject to FTC enforcement
extracted.subtask_description: Official FTC press release describing enforcement actions and the standards the Commission applies when companies advertise or deploy AI-powered products or schemes. Emphasizes what kinds of AI-related claims and practices are deceptive, unfair, or otherwise unlawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: No AI exemption from consumer protection laws
rubrics_metrics.description: “Using AI tools to trick, mislead, or defraud people is illegal... there is no AI exemption from the laws on the books.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC will apply existing consumer protection laws to AI-related products and claims (Operation AI Comply); firms cannot rely on ‘AI’ as a defense for deceptive or unfair conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims that AI substitutes for professional services must be supported
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies may not claim AI can substitute for licensed professionals (e.g., 'the world’s first robot lawyer' or 'sue for assault without a lawyer') unless they have evidence the service performs at the claimed professional level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FTC cited DoNotPay for promising replacement of human lawyers without testing or attorney involvement; proposed orders can prohibit claims that AI substitutes for professional services without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require testing/validation of AI outputs before marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing claims about an AI’s capabilities must be based on testing and validation demonstrating the outputs meet the advertised standard (e.g., equality to a human professional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC alleged DoNotPay 'did not conduct testing to determine whether its AI chatbot’s output was equal to the level of a human lawyer'; lack of validation can support deceptive-practice charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit tools marketed to generate fake consumer reviews or testimonials
rubrics_metrics.description: Selling or promoting services dedicated to generating consumer reviews/testimonials—particularly detailed, fabricated reviews—is unlawful if it results in false or deceptive marketplace content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC charged Rytr for a 'Testimonial & Review' generation feature that produced detailed, likely-false reviews; proposed order would bar advertising, promoting, marketing, or selling services dedicated to generating consumer reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earnings and income claims must be substantiated; no guaranteed profits
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertised earnings claims (e.g., 'five-figure monthly income', '7-figure business', '$100,000 per month in profit') must have a reasonable evidentiary basis; promises of guaranteed income are deceptive when unsupported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC complaints against Ascend Ecom, Ecommerce Empire Builders, and FBA Machine allege unsupported earnings claims that defrauded consumers; courts can halt such schemes and FTC enforcement targets these claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business opportunity schemes may be unlawful when material claims are false
rubrics_metrics.description: Schemes that charge large sums for training or storefronts while making false or unsupported material claims about likely outcomes (profitability, proprietary AI that ensures success) can be subject to enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC filed lawsuits and obtained receiverships where operators charged tens of thousands while failing to deliver promised outcomes; operators may face civil actions and asset control by courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot coerce consumers to remove negative reviews or withhold promised refunds/buybacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Pressuring customers to modify or delete negative reviews, or failing to honor advertised refund/guaranteed buyback promises, is unlawful and supports deception/unfairness claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC alleged Ascend pressured consumers to delete negative reviews and failed to honor guaranteed buybacks; such practices are cited as evidence of deceptive conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfair practices that 'pollute the marketplace' (e.g., mass fake reviews) are actionable
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing services that are likely to flood the marketplace with false content (such as mass-produced fake reviews) may be an unfair business practice harming consumers and honest competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC alleged Rytr’s review-generation service 'is likely to pollute the marketplace' and constitutes an unfair practice under the FTC Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims about proprietary AI/software powering business outcomes must be substantiated
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements that a proprietary algorithm or AI will 'maximize' success or is central to business performance must have evidentiary support and cannot be used as puffery to lure consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ecommerce Empire Builders' marketing claiming 'proprietary software and artificial intelligence to maximize clients’ business success' was alleged to lack evidence; unsupported technical-advantage claims can be deceptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of biometric/AI facial recognition requires reasonable safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Deploying facial recognition or other biometric AI technologies must include reasonable safeguards to protect consumers; claiming such use without safeguards can be unlawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC alleged Rite Aid used AI facial recognition 'without reasonable safeguards'; lack of safeguards can give rise to enforcement actions concerning privacy and unfair practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and algorithmic claims (e.g., DNA reports) must be truthful and substantiated
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims about accuracy, matching, or the use of AI algorithms in products such as genetic reports must reflect actual capabilities and be supported by evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC cited CRI Genetics for allegedly deceiving users about accuracy and AI use; misrepresentations about algorithmic performance can be actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special protections apply when marketing AI products to children or claiming AI moderation
rubrics_metrics.description: Products or apps marketed to children (or claiming AI safety/moderation) must actually implement appropriate moderation and comply with protections for minors; false safety claims are unlawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC alleged NGL Labs claimed to use AI moderation while unlawfully marketing an anonymous messaging app to children; truthful representations about moderation and child-directed safeguards are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebranding does not cure prior deceptive practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators who rebrand after complaints cannot escape liability; continuing the same deceptive business under a new name does not avoid enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTC alleged Rozenfeld rebranded Passive Scaling as FBA Machine after complaints; courts can halt rebranded schemes and enforcement continues despite name changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies may include monetary payments, consumer notices, and prohibitions on certain claims or services
rubrics_metrics.description: Consent orders and settlements can require payments to consumers, public notices to affected users, and bans on making certain future claims or offering certain services (e.g., review generators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoNotPay’s proposed order would require payment of $193,000, consumer notices about limitations, and prohibit making claims about substituting for a professional without evidence; Rytr’s proposed order would bar selling services dedicated to generating consumer reviews. Orders are subject to public comment via the Federal Register.
